summary: Forest Service 14x14 ground cab on Butler Peak above Big Bear Lake, built 1935; volunteer-staffed in season; reopened 2022 after storm-damage closure.

facts.design: Region 5 Plan BC-301 14 x 14 ft wooden ground house with catwalk, set on a blasted rock outcrop

staffing.status: volunteer-staffed by Southern California Mountain Foundation in the open season

access.note: open to visitors on a seasonal schedule, Memorial Day to November; dirt access road; high clearance recommended; snow can persist into July

visit.trail_note: drive up dirt Forest Roads 3N14, 2N13 and 2N13C from Highway 38 at Fawnskin; climb the stairs to the catwalk when the tower is staffed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register's Built field and the October 1935 newspaper report give 1935. The Register's description says the CCC built it in 1933, and a March 1934 report names workers from the City Creek camp. The story uses 1935 and reports the 1933 claim as the Register's own.
The Register gives 8,419 ft (2,566 m), the 1935 newspaper gives 8,502 feet, and the Mountains Foundation gives 8,535 ft. The story reports all three and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: Build year 1935 is supported by the Register Built field and the 1935 newspaper reports; the Register's 1933 CCC claim is the only dissent and is reported in the story. The brief's access was 'unknown' and is now public with a seasonal schedule. The 2025 season is the latest confirmed opening; 2026 status is unverified. Elevation is given three ways (8,419 / 8,502 / 8,535 ft) and the story shows all three. The 1970 Bear Fire spotting comes only from the Mountains Foundation page; no separate fire record was read. Checked 2026-10-08: the 8,502-foot passage is from the October 31, 1935 report; the 'so no tower' link is now attributed to the peak's elevation. The telephone and road line now says what the report says (a link to the Green Valley-Fawnskin truck trail). The Register's 2026 90th anniversary does not match a 1935 build year (1935 + 90 = 2025), so it may count from completion; the story reports the Register's wording without reconciling it.
